start_here: Say to your AI: "Find the spoken lines in my recordings that say all of some words, and say the file and time of each", with {"index_ids":["synthetic-said"],"query_text":"made-up words"}. It runs tool:find-words-said-in-my-recordings and answers {"index_ids":["synthetic-said"],"lines":[{"address":"/Sets/said.jsonl#0","file":"/Clips/made-up.m4a","start":0,"end":null,"text":"some made-up words here"}]}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours: it takes its input and keeps only its own rows (semantic-index-descriptor, ) through the records door.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Find the spoken lines in my recordings that say all of some words, and say the file and time of each", and give it index_ids (The index_id of each of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records to search together); query_text (The words to look for; every word longer than two letters must be in a line).
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:find-words-said-in-my-recordings and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Reads the vector sets of several of the person's semantic-index-descriptor records (index_ids) whose points_to names a text field, and returns, in the order the sets hold them, the lines that contain every word of query_text longer than two letters (case ignored), at most limit (8 when none is asked).
4. It reads and writes only its own rows through the records door: semantic-index-descriptor (records:list); undefined (read_file).
